report:
**Conclusion**  
The claim is **true**. The Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing) intrauterine system is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years.

**Evidence**  
According to official U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) prescribing information, Kyleena (a 19.5 mg levonorgestrel intrauterine system) is explicitly indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years. The system releases a low dose of progestin in the uterus over time and must be removed or replaced by the end of the fifth year if continued contraceptive protection is desired. 

The approval was based on data from Phase III clinical trials evaluating its safety and effectiveness. Clinical guidance documents note that while higher-dose levonorgestrel IUDs (such as Mirena or Liletta) have received approval for extended use past five years, Kyleena's duration is strictly limited to 5 years, as extended use beyond this duration has not been established.

**Sources**
* FDA Prescribing Information Label: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf
* DailyMed Package Insert: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080
* Drugs.com Kyleena Approval History: https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html
* NASPAG LARC Extended Use Guidelines: https://www.naspag.org/assets/docs/LARC+extended+use+talking+points.pdf
